children: The 21-member currency bloc posted a €16.1bn deficit in goods traded with the rest of the world, compared with a €10.7bn surplus in July and a €1.7bn deficit in August 2025.
Imports jumped 16.7% year-on-year to €243.8bn, significantly outpacing the 9.9% increase in exports to €227.7bn.
The deterioration came amid disruption to global energy supplies resulting from the war in the Middle East, with the eurozone's energy trade deficit widening to €26.7bn from €21.3bn a year earlier.
The balance of trade in machinery and vehicles also weakened sharply, swinging from a €7.2bn surplus in August 2025 to a €0.7bn deficit.
Across the first eight months of 2026, the eurozone recorded a cumulative trade deficit of €5.4bn, a sharp reversal from the €90.9bn surplus registered during the same period last year.
Exports increased 2.1% to €1.99trn over the eight-month period, while imports rose 7.3% to €2.0trn.
